s • AI Assistant
Absolutely — the easiest way to start is by choosing based on 2 things:



Sleep style


Sprawlers: rectangular beds


Curlers: Tough Oval Bolster or Tough Round Nesting


Leaners: Tough Bolster Beds


Destructive level


Heavy chewers: Chew Proof Armored beds


Mild chewers/diggers: Tough Ripstop line


Big/older dogs: orthopedic options add support



If you want, tell me your dog’s size, sleep style, and chewing habits and I’ll help narrow it down.

turns.q: Is there anything else a beginner needs to get started?
turns.replyTail:
hing else a beginner needs to get started?
K9 Ballistics • AI Assistant
Yes — a beginner mainly needs the right size and setup.



Measure your dog nose-to-tail and compare it to the bed’s sleeping area


If your dog likes to sprawl, add about 10 in. for extra room


For bolster beds, note the sleeping area can be smaller than the full footprint


If using a crate bed, use the included tie-downs


If you live somewhere hot, an elevated mesh bed can help with cooling

operly the very first time?

Most beds arrive as a rolled mattress + folded cover, so put the cover on first


Shake out pillow or bolster inserts to help them fluff faster
